p8/esc1283:1.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:1.text: Hi I am feeling quite sad today.

p8/esc1283:10.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:10.text: In that case, should you consider them as your friends?

p8/esc1283:11.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:11.text: Well they are the only friends I have and I have known them a long time. Do you think I should stop being friends with them ?

p8/esc1283:12.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:12.text: If someone is not friendly they are not real friend. You need to find someone who will stand by you no matter what..

p8/esc1283:13.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:13.text: Oh well that makes me feel sad too.  I will be saying goodbye to some long friendships. Do you think that is the only answer ?

p8/esc1283:14.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:14.text: Ok.. how about hosting them in your place for a gettogether..

p8/esc1283:15.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:15.text: Ok how do you think that would help me ?

p8/esc1283:16.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:16.text: They might open up if you are hosting .. people are generally nice to the host..

p8/esc1283:17.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:17.text: Yes that is true, it's a good idea.  I could also take the opportunity to tell them how I am feeling.

p8/esc1283:18.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:18.text: Good.. let's try that.. Anythign else I could help you with?

p8/esc1283:19.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:19.text: No you have been very helpful and I feel much better now I have a plan of action to address my problem. Thanks.

p8/esc1283:2.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:2.text: Ohh, sorry to hear that. Any partucular reason?

p8/esc1283:20.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:20.text: Thank you .. have a good day.

p8/esc1283:3.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:3.text: Yes I feel like my friends just don't care about me much at all.

p8/esc1283:4.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:4.text: You saying that your friend does not care about you any more. Is that correct?

p8/esc1283:5.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:5.text: Yes, when we get together all they want to do is talk about themselves. When I raise something that is bothering me they just ignore what I say and go back to what they want to talk about.

p8/esc1283:6.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:6.text: That's not good. You must be feeling left out.

p8/esc1283:7.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:7.text: Yes I feel left out and unsupported by them.

p8/esc1283:8.speaker: supporter
p8/esc1283:8.text: Any particular reason they are doing such thing?

p8/esc1283:9.speaker: seeker
p8/esc1283:9.text: Well I think they don't care about me and are just selfish about their needs.

p8/esc242:10.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:10.text: Wow--that does sound annoying that he will repeat the same pattern the next time.

p8/esc242:11.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:11.text: He will literally talk up to 10 minutes without letting you have a word in. As far as that advice, I have hung up, but he gets extremely offended easily.

p8/esc242:12.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:12.text: That sounds really difficult if he gets offended so easily. I find it hard to talk to some of those kinds of friends.

p8/esc242:13.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:13.text: I'm at my wits end. I tell him all the time. "You talk too much. You gotta stop talking at me. You gotta give the other person a turn. You gotta respect other's time."

p8/esc242:14.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:14.text: What do you get out of the friendship with this other person?

p8/esc242:15.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:15.text: Well, I've been friends with him for a long time. He's funny and can have interesting perspectives on things. Also, we have done a lot together in the past.

p8/esc242:16.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:16.text: That sounds like a lot that the two of you have been through. Were there other times that your friends was more equally responsive or attuned to you in conversations?

p8/esc242:17.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:17.text: Oh, yes, I have other friends in conversations who can take turns and understand the concept of time just fine.

p8/esc242:18.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:18.text: I just don't know what to do about this guy in particular. I still want to be his friend, but he just doesn't change.

p8/esc242:19.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:19.text: I wonder if there is anything nice you could do for yourself when you are talking to him that would make it easier to talk to him.

p8/esc242:2.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:2.text: I am decent. I am here because my friend talks way too much on the phone, and it frustrates me.

p8/esc242:20.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:20.text: Do you think I should just have a timer that goes off at 1 minute and let it beep in his face if he goes on for too long to train him like a monkey?

p8/esc242:21.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:21.text: I can see that you are feeling upset and angry when he talks so much and that is totally understandable.

p8/esc242:22.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:22.text: I just need a method. Talking to him is just not working.

p8/esc242:24.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:24.text: Would it hurt his feelings to use a timer like that? It may for some other people.

p8/esc242:25.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:25.text: Yea, but I might be able to slip some humour in there to take the edge off because it is so silly.

p8/esc242:26.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:26.text: Humor is really helpful for a lot of people.

p8/esc242:28.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:28.text: Sometimes, people draw or do something else distracting with their hands when talking to someone who dominates the conversation.

p8/esc242:29.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:29.text: So your option is to start just doing something else when he is talking? He might get the message in a subtle way?

p8/esc242:3.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:3.text: They never want to hang up, and the talk can literally go on for hours.

p8/esc242:30.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:30.text: Sometimes that is a less offensive way to retrain someone who is being obnoxious or dominant and yet who is easily offended. And, it can help preserve your sense of being grounded.

p8/esc242:31.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:31.text: The strategy works well for me with some of my family members who seem like they will never change. But, with distraction, I enjoy them all the more.

p8/esc242:32.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:32.text: This is true, and it isn't bade advice. Haha! That is funny. Yes, maybe I should find something to carry around with me that I can enjoy.

p8/esc242:33.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:33.text: I don't really like to draw...

p8/esc242:34.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:34.text: Is there anything else that you like to do that would be distracting while also letting you somewhat participate in the conversation?

p8/esc242:35.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:35.text: Yes, perhaps I should just use the internet when he starts talking too much.

p8/esc242:37.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:37.text: That sounds really helpful. Sometimes people also play phone games or with a fidget spinner. I like your idea of looking on the internet.

p8/esc242:38.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:38.text: This solves the problem in person, but it doesn't solve the talks over the phone, but it has been 15 minutes now and this has been helpful enough. Thank you for your solutions. You have been very supportive and kind to me

p8/esc242:39.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:39.text: I don't want to take up any more of your time. It has been a good conversation.

p8/esc242:4.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:4.text: It sounds like it would be quite frustrating for your friend to talk way too much on the phone.

p8/esc242:40.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:40.text: You are very welcome. I wish you all the best!

p8/esc242:5.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:5.text: No, he loves it! I'm the one who hates it.

p8/esc242:6.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:6.text: My goodness! How do they respond when you ask to end the conversation?

p8/esc242:7.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:7.text: I tell him, but he just doesn't get it. Or, he says he understands, but then just goes back to talking!

p8/esc242:8.speaker: seeker
p8/esc242:8.text: Or, he may finally end the talk, but the next time we talk, he will just do it all over again!

p8/esc242:9.speaker: supporter
p8/esc242:9.text: I wonder what it would be like for him if you hung up the phone even after he said he still wanted to talk.

p8/esc617:1.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:1.text: Hi there I was hoping you can help me.

p8/esc617:10.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:10.text: It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered.

p8/esc617:11.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:11.text: Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.

p8/esc617:12.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:12.text: In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.

p8/esc617:13.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:13.text: That's a good way to look at it.

p8/esc617:14.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:14.text: You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?

p8/esc617:16.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:16.text: Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

p8/esc617:17.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:17.text: That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.

p8/esc617:18.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:18.text: hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.

p8/esc617:19.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:19.text: It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways

p8/esc617:2.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:2.text: Sure. What can I help you with?

p8/esc617:20.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:20.text: I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.

p8/esc617:21.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:21.text: I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this.

p8/esc617:22.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:22.text: Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.

p8/esc617:3.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:3.text: Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?

p8/esc617:4.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:4.text: I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be.

p8/esc617:5.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:5.text: What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?

p8/esc617:6.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:6.text: Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.

p8/esc617:7.speaker: supporter
p8/esc617:7.text: Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?

p8/esc617:8.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:8.text: They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.

p8/esc617:9.speaker: seeker
p8/esc617:9.text: What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

p8/esc995:0.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:0.text: Hi there, how are you doing?

p8/esc995:1.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:1.text: IM HANGING IN THERE HOW ARE YOU?

p8/esc995:10.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:10.text: I think it is likely to have been noticed though, at least.

p8/esc995:11.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:11.text: Yes I agree it sounds like a really big problem, but what should i do?

p8/esc995:12.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:12.text: I think the best thing would be to be really honest with your employers and ask if you can have time off for professional help.

p8/esc995:14.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:14.text: Are you employers likely to be sympathetic?

p8/esc995:15.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:15.text: my main concern, that makes me fearful is being fired, and being the talk of the workplace

p8/esc995:16.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:16.text: Ah people do love to idly gossip don't they? I've been through that myself. I know it's hard to ignore them but it's best to try.

p8/esc995:17.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:17.text: My employer is an well known organization that employees over 3,000 people.

p8/esc995:18.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:18.text: I do not know if they can fire you if you have a legitimate medical problem though.

p8/esc995:19.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:19.text: Well you could always shame them if they unfairly fired you.

p8/esc995:2.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:2.text: I am okay. What would you like to talk to me about?

p8/esc995:20.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:20.text: Very good to know that I will look into it. It did not start overnight and I don't expect it to end overnight

p8/esc995:22.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:22.text: Thank you so much for your time.

p8/esc995:23.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:23.text: Large corporations are always over concerned about their images. (we have to talk for fifteen minutes :))

p8/esc995:24.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:24.text: oh ok I thought it was just for 10 lines, lol

p8/esc995:25.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:25.text: but none the less, there are people really going through that scenario I just portrayex

p8/esc995:26.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:26.text: naw there's a time thing too :). Anyway, what sort of therapy do you think would be appropriate for you?

p8/esc995:27.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:27.text: To be honest, and I mean this sincerely, I've been through it :(

p8/esc995:28.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:28.text: I believe rehabilitative therapy would be best

p8/esc995:29.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:29.text: It can be very expensive though. In my country you can get it for free but there's a long waiting list.

p8/esc995:3.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:3.text: Well, i have a problem with drinking alcoholI am so scared my job will find out

p8/esc995:30.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:30.text: I have hads  a few drinks often but never abused it. thankfully.

p8/esc995:31.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:31.text: Well here you might can get help for free, but it does have to be paid back

p8/esc995:33.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:33.text: Are you in the US? Our healthcare system is a little less rigid here I think (UK)

p8/esc995:34.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:34.text: Yes Im in the United States (Alabama)

p8/esc995:35.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:35.text: I heard of the UK so many times but truthfully I know nothing about it

p8/esc995:36.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:36.text: Ah you are a long way away from me. I hope that you do manage to sort out your problems though and definitely do talk to your employers

p8/esc995:37.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:37.text: Ah it's quite nice here. We pay for healthcare out of our taxes so it's free at source.

p8/esc995:38.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:38.text: I will eventually get the courage to, I know how people talk around here, especially in the South

p8/esc995:39.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:39.text: Gossipy people are the worst. Just remind yourself that they all have skeletons in their closets too

p8/esc995:4.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:4.text: Do you drink when you are at work?

p8/esc995:41.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:41.text: Well anyway, I hope I have been able to offer your  some useful advice. I wish you all of the very best in the future.

p8/esc995:42.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:42.text: I think also the best thing to do is to talk to great people like you

p8/esc995:43.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:43.text: (can you press quit first and do the survey as I am not able to do it from my side)

p8/esc995:5.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:5.text: I have started calling in atleast twice as week.

p8/esc995:6.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:6.text: I have started drinking at work close to the end of my shift in the bathroom

p8/esc995:7.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:7.text: That does sound like it might be a big problem. How are  your employers reacting?

p8/esc995:8.speaker: supporter
p8/esc995:8.text: It sounds like you have a big problem that needs professional help, would you agree?

p8/esc995:9.speaker: seeker
p8/esc995:9.text: They have not mentioned anything to me yet.

p8/p8_conv_1:0.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:0.text: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?

p8/p8_conv_1:1.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:1.text: Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.

p8/p8_conv_1:10.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:10.text: That makes it even harder when it's unexpected. Was there anyone at the gathering who you felt did listen or understand?

p8/p8_conv_1:11.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:11.text: I think one of my friends was trying, but got caught up in someone else’s conversation. It wasn’t like they ignored me on purpose.

p8/p8_conv_1:12.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:12.text: It sounds like they had a lot going on at the time. But still, it's important that they realize how that affected you.

p8/p8_conv_1:13.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:13.text: Yeah, I hope I can talk to them about how I felt. I'm just not sure how to bring it up without making it awkward.

p8/p8_conv_1:14.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:14.text: It's definitely a delicate subject, but expressing how you feel is also important. Maybe you could start by mentioning how much their support means to you?

p8/p8_conv_1:15.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:15.text: That's a good idea. I guess I could tell them that it would really mean a lot to me if they could be there for me when I need it.

p8/p8_conv_1:16.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:16.text: That sounds like a thoughtful way to start the conversation. Remember, real friends will want to support you when they know something's up.

p8/p8_conv_1:17.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:17.text: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps to talk it through and feel a bit more prepared.

p8/p8_conv_1:18.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:18.text: Anytime, Jimmy. I'm here for you if you need to chat more. You're doing great by taking the steps to communicate how you feel.

p8/p8_conv_1:19.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:19.text: Thanks, it means a lot. I'll let you know how it goes.

p8/p8_conv_1:2.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:2.text: I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?

p8/p8_conv_1:3.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:3.text: Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.

p8/p8_conv_1:4.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:4.text: That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?

p8/p8_conv_1:5.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:5.text: I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.

p8/p8_conv_1:6.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:6.text: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.

p8/p8_conv_1:7.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:7.text: Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.

p8/p8_conv_1:8.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_1:8.text: Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?

p8/p8_conv_1:9.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_1:9.text: Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.

p8/p8_conv_24:0.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_24:0.text: Hey Jimmy, how have you been doing lately?

p8/p8_conv_24:1.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_24:1.text: Hey, I'm okay, I guess. I've started journaling daily. Thought it might help me make sense of everything.

p8/p8_conv_24:2.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_24:2.text: That's a great step. Writing things down can help untangle what's going on inside. How's it been for you so far?

p8/p8_conv_24:3.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_24:3.text: It's been... enlightening, but also a bit heavy. I didn't realize how many emotions I've been bottling up.

p8/p8_conv_24:4.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_24:4.text: I can imagine. Opening that bottle can be tough. Have you discovered anything about yourself through journaling?

p8/p8_conv_24:5.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_24:5.text: Yeah, I've noticed a pattern of avoiding conversations that make me uncomfortable. I guess I've been doing that a lot.

p8/p8_conv_24:6.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_24:6.text: Recognizing those patterns is a big first step. It shows you're gaining clarity. Have any specific situations come to mind?

p8/p8_conv_24:7.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_24:7.text: Well, my recent move to Sydney was partly because I felt trapped by my past here in Canberra. Wanted a fresh start, but I miss some things too.

p8/p8_conv_2:0.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:0.text: Hey George, it's really good to catch up with you. How have you been?

p8/p8_conv_2:1.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:1.text: Hey Jimmy! It's great to hear from you. I've been doing alright, just busy with work. How about you? What's been going on?

p8/p8_conv_2:10.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:10.text: I guess there's a lot, but lately, I'm really worried about my job. I've been having trouble managing things because of... well, an alcohol problem.

p8/p8_conv_2:11.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:11.text: That's a big thing to carry alone. Admitting you have a problem is a significant first step. You're really brave for acknowledging it.

p8/p8_conv_2:12.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:12.text: Thanks. It took me a while to come to terms with it. I'm worried if I don't get a handle on it, I might lose my job.

p8/p8_conv_2:13.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:13.text: That concern is definitely valid. Are there specific steps you're thinking of taking to manage it?

p8/p8_conv_2:14.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:14.text: I've actually started seeking professional help. It's scary, but I feel a bit more hopeful having someone to guide me.

p8/p8_conv_2:15.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:15.text: That’s really proactive, Jimmy. Having professional support can make a huge difference. How are you finding it so far?

p8/p8_conv_2:16.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:16.text: It's early days, but I feel like I'm starting to understand more about why I drink the way I do. It's hard work, though.

p8/p8_conv_2:17.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:17.text: Facing these things can be intense, but it sounds like you're gaining some valuable insights. That's progress.

p8/p8_conv_2:18.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:18.text: Yeah, I guess so. It's nice to hear that from someone else, though. It reinforces that I'm doing the right thing.

p8/p8_conv_2:19.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:19.text: Absolutely, you're on the right path. Remember, it's okay to lean on friends for support too. I'm here whenever you need to talk.

p8/p8_conv_2:2.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:2.text: Well, things haven't been the easiest lately. I feel like I'm kind of stuck in a bit of a rut.

p8/p8_conv_2:20.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:20.text: Thanks, George. It means a lot to have you in my corner. I'll definitely reach out more often.

p8/p8_conv_2:21.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:21.text: Anytime, Jimmy. We'll get through this together. Just take it one step at a time, and keep focusing on the positive changes you're making.

p8/p8_conv_2:3.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:3.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Want to talk more about what's been going on? I'm here to listen.

p8/p8_conv_2:4.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:4.text: Thanks, I really appreciate it. You know, it's been tough feeling like my friends don't take me seriously when I try to open up.

p8/p8_conv_2:5.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:5.text: That sounds frustrating and isolating. It's important to feel heard and supported. What happened?

p8/p8_conv_2:6.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:6.text: A few weeks back, I hosted a gathering and tried talking about some things that have been on my mind, but it seemed like no one was really listening.

p8/p8_conv_2:7.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:7.text: It must have felt pretty hurtful to be ignored, especially when you needed support.

p8/p8_conv_2:8.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_2:8.text: Yeah, it really was. It's made me hesitant to bring up how I'm feeling again, even though I know I need to talk about it.

p8/p8_conv_2:9.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_2:9.text: It's understandable to feel that way after being dismissed. Have you thought about what you'd most like to share?

p8/p8_conv_3:0.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:0.text: Hey Jimmy, good to hear from you. How have you been doing lately?

p8/p8_conv_3:1.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:1.text: Hi George. I've been okay, I guess. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster recently.

p8/p8_conv_3:10.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:10.text: That makes sense. It sounds like you’re finding new ways to address things that were weighing you down.

p8/p8_conv_3:11.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:11.text: Yeah, I hope so. I just worry about the process, you know? What if I can't handle it?

p8/p8_conv_3:12.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:12.text: It's normal to feel that way, Jimmy. Recovery is a journey, not a sprint. It's okay to have doubts.

p8/p8_conv_3:13.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:13.text: I appreciate that. I do want to keep going, but the fear of failing is there.

p8/p8_conv_3:14.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:14.text: Fear is natural, but remember you've already taken the first step. You have the support to go through this.

p8/p8_conv_3:15.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:15.text: Thanks, that helps. The people at the meeting were welcoming, which made a difference.

p8/p8_conv_3:16.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:16.text: That's really good to hear. It's important to feel supported and understood in a group like that.

p8/p8_conv_3:17.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:17.text: Yeah, it felt different from trying to talk with my current friends. I think I need this new beginning.

p8/p8_conv_3:18.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:18.text: It sounds like you're on the right path, Jimmy. I'm here for you, whatever you need.

p8/p8_conv_3:19.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:19.text: That really means a lot to me, George. Thanks for being there.

p8/p8_conv_3:2.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:2.text: I get that. You've had a lot on your plate. What's been going on?

p8/p8_conv_3:3.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:3.text: Well, I went to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for the first time yesterday.

p8/p8_conv_3:4.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:4.text: That's a huge step, Jimmy. I'm really proud of you for taking it. How did it feel?

p8/p8_conv_3:5.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:5.text: Intimidating, honestly. Walking in there, not knowing anyone, feeling vulnerable... it wasn't easy.

p8/p8_conv_3:6.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:6.text: I can only imagine how tough that must have been. But you did it, and that says a lot about your courage.

p8/p8_conv_3:7.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:7.text: Thanks, George. I kept thinking about that day at the gathering when I tried to talk to everyone but felt ignored.

p8/p8_conv_3:8.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_3:8.text: I remember you mentioning that. It must've been so frustrating to feel unheard by people you consider friends.

p8/p8_conv_3:9.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_3:9.text: Yeah, it was. I guess that's part of why I pushed myself to try something different, like the AA meeting.

p8/p8_conv_4:0.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:0.text: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How have the AA meetings been going?

p8/p8_conv_4:1.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:1.text: Hey there. Well, surprisingly, they've been quite helpful. I met someone there, Bob, who's kind of going through the same issues.

p8/p8_conv_4:10.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:10.text: Acknowledging those patterns is a huge step. It's brave of you to face those issues head-on.

p8/p8_conv_4:11.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:11.text: Thanks. I just sometimes worry if I’m too late, you know? That I might lose everything.

p8/p8_conv_4:12.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:12.text: It's normal to feel that way, but you’re taking action now, and that’s important. It's never too late to make a change.

p8/p8_conv_4:13.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:13.text: Yeah, you're right. I guess I just have to keep reminding myself of that.

p8/p8_conv_4:14.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:14.text: Absolutely. And remember, you're not alone in this. Bob and others at AA are there for you, and so am I.

p8/p8_conv_4:15.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:15.text: I appreciate that. It's comforting to have a supportive net. I need to hold onto that.

p8/p8_conv_4:16.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:16.text: You're building a strong foundation, Jimmy. Just keep taking it one day at a time.

p8/p8_conv_4:17.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:17.text: Thanks. It helps to break it down like that. I’ll try to focus on each day and not get overwhelmed.

p8/p8_conv_4:18.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:18.text: That sounds like a solid plan. You've got this, Jimmy. Remember, progress is progress, no matter how small.

p8/p8_conv_4:19.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:19.text: Thanks a lot. Your words mean a lot to me right now. I’ll keep them in mind.

p8/p8_conv_4:2.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:2.text: That's great to hear. It must feel nice to have someone who truly understands what you're going through.

p8/p8_conv_4:20.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:20.text: Anytime. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Keep me posted on how things go, okay?

p8/p8_conv_4:21.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:21.text: I will. Thanks again, really. I'll talk to you soon.

p8/p8_conv_4:3.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:3.text: Yeah, definitely. It feels different from when I talked to my other friends. They just didn't get it, you know?

p8/p8_conv_4:4.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:4.text: I remember you mentioned feeling dismissed by them before. It sounds like finding someone who empathizes really makes a difference.

p8/p8_conv_4:5.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:5.text: Exactly. With Bob, I don't feel judged. We can share our stories, and it's like this unspoken bond.

p8/p8_conv_4:6.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:6.text: That unspoken understanding can be so powerful. Have you been able to open up more because of it?

p8/p8_conv_4:7.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:7.text: A bit. It's scary, but I’ve been sharing more of my feelings, and it feels freeing somehow. The fear of being judged or not being taken seriously is starting to fade.

p8/p8_conv_4:8.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_4:8.text: That sounds like real progress, Jimmy. Have you felt any changes in your day-to-day life since attending these meetings?

p8/p8_conv_4:9.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_4:9.text: Yeah, definitely. I've started to recognize some patterns in my behavior and why I turned to alcohol. It's frightening to see, but it’s the first step, I guess.

p8/p8_conv_5:0.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:0.text: Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?

p8/p8_conv_5:1.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:1.text: Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.

p8/p8_conv_5:10.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:10.text: It's disheartening when communication doesn't feel effective. Have you been able to talk to anyone else about this?

p8/p8_conv_5:11.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:11.text: I did mention it to my new friend from the AA meetings. It helps having someone who gets the struggle.

p8/p8_conv_5:12.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:12.text: It's great that you have that connection. How are things going with AA?

p8/p8_conv_5:13.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:13.text: It's been eye-opening and comforting, but the work stress isn't helping.

p8/p8_conv_5:14.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:14.text: Balancing everything can be challenging. Would you consider discussing this with your manager again with maybe different strategies in mind?

p8/p8_conv_5:15.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:15.text: I've thought about it. Maybe writing down my points beforehand could help.

p8/p8_conv_5:16.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:16.text: That sounds like a solid plan. It might help make sure you’re heard.

p8/p8_conv_5:17.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:17.text: Thanks. I just need to find the courage to approach him again.

p8/p8_conv_5:18.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:18.text: You have that courage, Jimmy. Remember how you stepped up to attend those AA meetings?

p8/p8_conv_5:19.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:19.text: Yeah, you're right. If I did that, I can do this too.

p8/p8_conv_5:2.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:2.text: I'm here for you. Do you want to talk about it?

p8/p8_conv_5:20.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:20.text: Absolutely. You're stronger than you realize. I'm here to back you.

p8/p8_conv_5:21.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:21.text: Thanks for saying that. It means a lot.

p8/p8_conv_5:22.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:22.text: Anytime. Let me know how it goes, okay?

p8/p8_conv_5:23.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:23.text: I will. Thanks again for listening.

p8/p8_conv_5:24.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:24.text: Always here for you, Jimmy. Take care.

p8/p8_conv_5:3.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:3.text: Thanks. Yeah, I had a disagreement with my manager at work today.

p8/p8_conv_5:5.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:5.text: We didn't see eye to eye on what should be prioritized. It just made me anxious.

p8/p8_conv_5:6.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:6.text: Conflict like that can be really stressful. Did you get a chance to express your perspective?

p8/p8_conv_5:7.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:7.text: I tried, but it felt like he wasn't really listening. It reminded me of when I felt ignored by friends before.

p8/p8_conv_5:8.speaker: supporter
p8/p8_conv_5:8.text: I remember you sharing that experience at the gathering you hosted. It's tough feeling sidelined.

p8/p8_conv_5:9.speaker: seeker
p8/p8_conv_5:9.text: Exactly. It feels like no matter where I turn, I'm not being heard.
